title: Abdominal Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is an older man with chronic osteoarthritis who presents with epigastric abdominal pain of one week's duration. History reveals extensive, prolonged use of oral ibuprofen for knee pain. NSAIDs block both COX-1 and COX-2, impairing gastric prostaglandin production and disrupting mucosal defense — this is classic NSAID-induced gastropathy. Symptoms began one week ago and the patient is medically stable. Conservative management is key: discontinue NSAIDs, start a proton-pump inhibitor, and follow up in 2-4 weeks. If no improvement with conservative therapy, then EGD would be indicated, but ordering it now loses points — the USMLE tests restraint from invasive testing. H. pylori should be ruled out. For his osteoarthritis, switch to acetaminophen and/or topical diclofenac gel rather than oral NSAIDs. Address modifiable risk factors: smoking cessation and alcohol avoidance.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: General Appearance
stacks.finding: Determine how sick the patient looks.

stacks.label: H. pylori testing (antibody / urea breath test / stool antigen)
stacks.finding: H. pylori should be ruled out as cause of gastritis.

stacks.label: Occult blood, stool
stacks.finding: Rule out GI bleed. Negative in this case. Not required — could be gathered from physical exam.

stacks.label: Endoscopy, upper gastrointestinal (EGD)
stacks.finding: EGD should ONLY be done after conservative treatment has failed for 2-4 weeks. Ordering now loses points — tests restraint from invasive testing.

stacks.label: PPI (Omeprazole / Lansoprazole / Pantoprazole / Esomeprazole) or H2 blocker
stacks.finding: Decrease stomach acid to treat NSAID-induced gastritis. PPIs preferred over H2 blockers.

stacks.label: Acetaminophen / Topical diclofenac
stacks.finding: For osteoarthritis pain: Tylenol first-line. If ineffective, topical diclofenac gel is preferred initial pharmacologic therapy. Avoid oral NSAIDs and opioids.

stacks.label: Consult, orthopedic surgery
stacks.finding: Long-term solution for osteoarthritis — surgical evaluation.

stacks.label: Advise patient, no NSAIDs
stacks.finding: Extensive NSAID use caused this gastritis. Must discontinue oral NSAIDs.

stacks.label: Advise patient, no alcohol
stacks.finding: Alcohol exacerbates acute gastritis — avoid until symptoms resolve.

stacks.label: Instruct patient, smoking cessation
stacks.finding: Smoking contributes to gastritis and peptic ulcer disease.

stacks.label: Tdap vaccine
stacks.finding: Tdap every 10 years. No history given.

physical_exam.abdominal: Epigastric tenderness. No peritoneal signs. No rebound/guarding.
physical_exam.musculoskeletal: Osteoarthritic knee changes — source of chronic NSAID use.

decoys.label: EGD / Upper endoscopy
decoys.reason_wrong: Should only be ordered after 2-4 weeks of failed conservative therapy. The USMLE tests your ability to restrain from ordering invasive tests in stable patients.

decoys.label: Opioids for chronic OA pain
decoys.reason_wrong: Opioids are not first-line for chronic osteoarthritis. Acetaminophen and topical NSAIDs are preferred. Avoid long-term opioid prescribing.

decoys.label: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
decoys.reason_wrong: No evidence of infection. H. pylori negative. Gastritis is chemical (NSAID-induced), not infectious.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Extensive ibuprofen use = NSAID-induced gastropathy. NSAIDs block COX-1 → decreased gastric prostaglandins → impaired mucosal defense. This is the most common cause of acute gastritis.
First-line: discontinue offending agent + acid suppression (PPI > H2 blocker). Follow up in 2-4 weeks. EGD only if no improvement.

teach_me_steps.order: Switch OA treatment: acetaminophen + topical diclofenac
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Acetaminophen first-line for OA. Topical diclofenac gel preferred over oral NSAIDs. Avoid opioids for chronic use.
Smoking and alcohol exacerbate gastritis and PUD. Address modifiable risk factors.

case_summary: NSAID-induced acute gastritis from chronic ibuprofen use for OA. Conservative management: stop NSAIDs, start PPI, switch to acetaminophen/topical diclofenac. Avoid EGD unless fails 2-4 weeks of conservative therapy. Office management.
